advanced-filter-description: Advanced Filter allows to write a string containing following operators: == != <= >= && || ( ) A space is used as a separator between the Operators. You can filter for all Custom Fields by typing their names and values. For Example: Field1 == Value1. Note: If fields or values contains spaces, you need to encapsulate them into single quotes. For Example: 'Field 1' == 'Value 1'. For single control characters (' \/) to be skipped, you can use \. For example: Field1 == I\'m. Also you can combine multiple conditions. For Example: F1 == V1 || F1 == V2. Normally all operators are interpreted from left to right. You can change the order by placing brackets. For Example: F1 == V1 && ( F2 == V2 || F2 == V3 ). Also you can search text fields using regex: F1 == /Tes.*/i

import-board-instruction-kanboard: Paste a Kanboard export JSON: an object with "columns" (or tasks carrying column_name) and a "tasks" array (title, description, column_name, swimlane_name, date_due, owner, tags). Columns become lists and tasks become cards.
import-board-instruction-deck: Paste a NextCloud Deck board JSON (a board with "stacks", each stack carrying its "cards"). Stacks become lists and cards become cards.
import-board-instruction-openproject: Paste an OpenProject work-packages collection JSON (GET /api/v3/work_packages). Statuses become lists and work packages become cards.
import-board-instruction-issues: Paste a __sourceName__ issues JSON array (__endpoint__). Issues become cards grouped into Open / Closed lists.
import-board-instruction-asana: Paste an Asana tasks export JSON ({ "data": [...] } from the Asana export or GET /tasks). Tasks are grouped into sections (memberships); completed tasks go to Done.
import-board-instruction-zenkit: Paste a ZenKit list export JSON ({ "title", "stages":[...], "items":[...] }). Stages become lists and items become cards.
import-board-instruction-markdown: Paste a markdown task list (the convention markdown-kanban tools such as Obsidian Kanban use): "## List name" headings, with "- [ ]"/"- [x]" items underneath. Headings become lists and items become cards; a plain bulleted list with no checkboxes also imports, as open cards.
import-board-instruction-leo: Paste a Leo outline (.leo file). Top-level nodes become lists, their children become cards with the node body as the description, and deeper nodes become checklists. Marked nodes import as done.
import-board-instruction-opml: Paste an OPML outline, as Workflowy, Dynalist, OmniOutliner, Logseq and other outliners export it. Top-level items become lists, their children become cards with the note as the description, and deeper items become checklists. Completed items import as done.
import-board-instruction-orgmode: Paste an Org mode file, as Emacs, Orgzly or Beorg write it. Top-level headings become lists and second-level headings become cards. TODO and DONE, priorities, tags, SCHEDULED, DEADLINE and CLOSED are kept, and checkboxes and deeper headings become checklists.
import-board-instruction-todotxt: Paste a todo.txt file: one task per line, as the todo.txt app and compatible apps write it. Completed tasks ("x") go to Done, +project and @context become labels, (A) becomes a priority label, and due: and t: become due and start dates.
import-board-instruction-taskwarrior: Paste the output of task export: a JSON array, or one task per line. Completed tasks go to Done, project and priority become labels, annotations become comments, and depends becomes blocked-by dependencies.
import-board-instruction-focalboard: Unzip the .boardarchive file and paste a board's board.jsonl, with or without its version line. The board view's group-by property becomes the lists, other select properties become labels, text and checkbox blocks become the description and a checklist, and comments are kept. Images and attachments are not imported.
import-board-instruction-todoist: In Todoist, open the project, choose the ⋯ menu at its top right, then Manage data > Export as CSV, and paste the CSV file. Sections become lists, tasks become cards, sub-tasks become a checklist, notes become comments, and @labels and priorities p1 to p3 become labels.
import-board-instruction-planner: In Microsoft Planner, open the plan, choose the ⋯ menu next to its name, then Export as Excel (in classic Planner: Export plan to Excel), and choose that .xlsx file. Buckets become lists and tasks become cards, with their assignees, dates, labels, checklist and description; Progress, Priority and Completed By become custom fields.
import-board-instruction-azuredevops: In Azure DevOps, open Boards, then Queries, run a query that shows the columns you want, and choose Export to CSV; choose that .csv file. Board Column (or State) becomes the lists and Board Lane the swimlanes; work items become cards with their type and tags as labels, Assigned To, dates, description and parent, and the other columns become custom fields.
import-board-instruction-mslists: In Microsoft Lists, open the list, choose Export, then Export to CSV, and choose that .csv file. The Status column (or Progress) becomes the lists and each item a card, with its title, description, people, dates and tags; the other columns become custom fields.
import-board-instruction-msproject: In Microsoft Project, choose File, then Save As, with the type XML Format (*.xml), and choose that file. Summary tasks become swimlanes and tasks become cards in Not started, In progress or Completed, with their dates, notes, resources, subtasks and predecessors.
import-board-instruction-outlook: In Outlook, drag messages to a folder on your computer, or save them with File, then Save As, as Outlook Message Format (*.msg). Choose one .msg file, or a .zip of .msg and .eml files. Each conversation becomes a card in Board View / Email, with its replies as comments and its attachments as files.
import-board-instruction-meistertask: In MeisterTask, click the project name, choose Export project and export the CSV, then paste it. Sections become lists and tasks become cards, with their notes, due date, assignee and tags; completed tasks keep their completion date. A CSV written for MeisterTask's own import works too.
import-board-instruction-obsidian: In Obsidian, open the Kanban board's file as Markdown (or open the .md file in a text editor), then paste all of it. Lanes become lists with their card limits, cards keep their tags, dates, priority, fields and checklist, and the Archive becomes archived cards.
import-board-instruction-linear: In Linear, export the issues as CSV (Settings, Import / Export, Export data, or a view's export), then paste the CSV. Statuses become lists, teams become swimlanes, and issues become cards with their assignee, labels, dates, parent issue, priority, estimate, project and cycle.
import-board-instruction-ticktick: In TickTick, open Settings, Account, Backup & Import and generate a backup, then paste the CSV file. Each TickTick list becomes a swimlane and its columns become lists; tasks keep their tags, dates, checklist, priority and subtasks.
import-board-instruction-clickup: In ClickUp, export the tasks as CSV (Settings, Imports / Exports, Export Items, or a List or Table view's export with all columns), then paste the CSV. Statuses become lists, ClickUp lists become swimlanes, and tasks become cards with their subtasks, assignees, tags, dates, priority and time.
import-board-instruction-nullboard: In Nullboard, open the board, choose Export this board... from the menu, open the .nbx file in a text editor and paste its contents. Lists become lists and notes become cards: a note's first line is the card title and the rest its description. A raw note gets the label raw. A file with several boards imports its first board.
import-board-instruction-kanri: In Kanri, open Import & Export and choose Export individual board (or Export all data), then paste the .json file. Columns become lists and cards become cards, with their description, due date, tags and colors; a card's tasks become a checklist. From an all-data export the first board is imported.
import-board-instruction-planka: Type the address of your Planka (for example https://planka.example.com), your Planka username and password, then press List. They are used only to fetch the board and are not stored. Choose a board and press Fetch: WeKan reads it from Planka's API, with its lists, cards, descriptions, due dates, labels, members, task lists and comments, then continue the import as usual. Cards in Planka's archive are imported archived; attachments and cards in the trash are not imported.
import-board-instruction-mstodo: In Microsoft Graph Explorer (developer.microsoft.com/graph/graph-explorer), sign in, consent to the Tasks.Read permission and copy the token from the Access token tab. Paste it here and click List; the token is used for this fetch only and is not stored. Choose all lists or one list and click Fetch. Each To Do list becomes a list and each task a card, with its notes, due and start dates, steps as a checklist, categories as labels, high importance and status as labels; completed tasks are archived. Reminders and repeats are not imported.
import-board-instruction-onenote: In Microsoft Graph Explorer (developer.microsoft.com/graph/graph-explorer), sign in, consent to the Notes.Read permission and copy the token from the Access token tab. Paste it here and click List; the token is used for this fetch only and is not stored. Choose a notebook and click Fetch. Sections become lists and pages become cards, with their text, to-do boxes as a checklist and subpages as subtasks.
import-board-instruction-teams: Paste a Microsoft Graph access token with Chat.Read (from Graph Explorer, a work or school account) and click List, then choose a chat or channel and click Fetch; the token is not stored. Or choose a file: the .tar of your personal export from teams.live.com/dataexport, or a .json of chat messages. Each chat becomes a card in Board View / Chat, its messages the comments.
import-board-instruction-sandstorm: In Sandstorm, open the __app__ grain, choose Download backup in the grain's top bar, and choose that .zip file. The grain's content becomes a board, its items cards with what the app keeps of them. Choose the app the grain is of: a grain of another app is refused, and says which app it is.
import-board-instruction-kanbanflow: In KanbanFlow, open the board's menu, choose Settings → API & Webhooks and copy the board's API token. Paste the token here, click List, choose the board and click Fetch; the token is used for that fetch only and is not stored. Columns become lists and swimlanes stay swimlanes; tasks keep their description, color, labels, due date, subtasks as a checklist, time spent, estimate, people and comments.
import-board-instruction-basecamp: Type your Basecamp account ID (the number after basecamp.com/ in the address) and an access token (from an OAuth 2 app registered at launchpad.37signals.com, or one an existing integration already has), click List, choose a project and click Fetch. The token is used for that fetch only and is not stored. Each card table becomes a swimlane with its columns as lists, and the to-do lists become a To-dos swimlane; cards and to-dos keep their text, dates, assignees and comments, a card's steps become a checklist, and completed to-dos are archived.
import-board-instruction-googletasks: Get an access token from the OAuth 2.0 Playground: under Tasks API v1 select tasks.readonly, click Authorize APIs, then Exchange authorization code for tokens, and copy the access token. Paste it here and click List, choose all task lists or one, then Fetch. The token is used for this fetch only and is not stored. Task lists become lists and tasks become cards, with their notes, links and due date; subtasks become a checklist and completed tasks are imported archived.
import-board-instruction-googlekeep: Google Keep's API is for Google Workspace accounts only. Get an OAuth 2.0 access token with the scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/keep.readonly (in the OAuth 2.0 Playground if your Workspace admin allows it, or from a service account with domain-wide delegation), paste it, click List and then Fetch. The token is used for this fetch only and is not stored. Text notes become cards in the list Notes, and checklist notes become cards in the list Lists with their items as a checklist. Trashed notes, attachments and sharing are not imported.
api-import-desc: Fetch it from the service with your own account. What you type here is used for this fetch only and is not stored.
api-import-fetched: Fetched. Check the members below and import.
api-import-nothing: There is nothing to import with this account.
import-board-instruction-pivotal: In Pivotal Tracker, open the project's MORE tab and choose Export CSV (or select stories and choose Bulk Actions, CSV), then paste the CSV. Each story state becomes a list and stories become cards, with their type and labels, owners, requester, dates, comments, tasks and blockers; Estimate becomes Story points and iterations become sprints.
import-board-instruction-tasksorg: In Tasks.org, open Settings, Backups and choose Export tasks, then paste the contents of that .json file. Lists become lists and tasks become cards, with their notes, tags, dates, comments and subtasks; completed tasks keep their completion date, and priority becomes a custom field.
import-board-instruction-monday: In monday.com, open the board menu, choose More actions and Export board to Excel (with updates and subitems if you like), then choose that .xlsx file. The Status column becomes lists and groups become swimlanes; people, dates, timeline and tags keep their places, other columns become custom fields and updates become comments.
import-board-instruction-superproductivi: In Super Productivity, open Settings, then Sync & Backup, choose Export Data and paste the contents of the sp-backup .json file. Each project becomes a swimlane and tasks become cards in To Do, In Progress, Backlog or Done, with their notes, tags, due date, time spent and sub-tasks; archived tasks become archived cards.
import-board-instruction-taiga: In Taiga, open Admin > Project > Export and download the project dump (unpack a .json.gz file first), then paste its JSON. User story statuses become lists, user stories become cards with their tasks as subtasks, epics and issues get swimlanes of their own, and sprints, tags, comments and custom attributes come along. Attachments are not imported.
import-board-instruction-vikunja: In Vikunja, open Settings, choose Data Export and download the .zip file it sends you, then choose that file, or paste the data.json inside it. Kanban buckets become lists and tasks become cards, with their labels, assignees, dates, description, task lists as checklists and comments; priority, percent done and done become custom fields. Attachments are not imported.
import-board-instruction-quire: In Quire, open the project menu and choose Export CSV, then paste the CSV. Statuses become lists and tasks become cards, with their subtasks as child cards, assignees, tags as labels, start, due and completed dates, description and priority as a custom field. Comments and attachments are not in Quire's CSV.
import-board-instruction-wrike: In Wrike, export a project or folder to Excel, or fill in Wrike's Excel import template, then choose that .xlsx file. Folder and project rows become swimlanes, Status becomes lists and tasks become cards, with their Key, parent task, assignees, start and end dates, dependencies and description; Priority, Duration and other columns become custom fields.
import-board-instruction-teamwork: In Teamwork.com, fill in the Excel task import template (Tasklist, Task, Description, Assign to, Start date, Due date, Priority, Estimated time, Tags, Status) and save it as .xlsx, then choose that file. Task lists become lists and tasks become cards; a task starting with -, # or > becomes a subtask of the task above it (--, ## or >> one level deeper). Assignees, dates and tags keep their places; Priority, Estimated time and Complete become custom fields.
import-board-instruction-businessmap: In Businessmap (formerly Kanbanize), open Advanced Search, choose Configure results to pick the columns, download the Excel file, then choose that .xlsx file. Columns are read by their English names (Title, Column, Lane, Owner, Deadline ...): if your account uses another language, rename the header row to English first. Column becomes lists and Lane swimlanes; owners, tags, color, dates, comments and parent links keep their places, and Priority, Size, Type and other columns become custom fields.
import-board-instruction-redmine: In Redmine, open the project's Issues, choose Also available in: CSV at the bottom of the list, pick the columns (All columns, with Description) and export, then paste the CSV. Redmine names the columns in your language, so set your language to English in My account before exporting. Each status becomes a list and issues become cards, with the tracker as a label, assignee, author, dates, parent task and related issues; priority, category, target version, estimated time, % Done and custom fields become custom fields.
import-board-instruction-notion: In Notion, open the database as a full page, choose ••• and Export, pick Markdown & CSV, and choose the .zip file it downloads, or one database CSV from it, or paste that CSV. A column named Status becomes the lists (without one, the first column that looks like a select does, and the import report says which); rows become cards with their title, tags as labels, people as members, dates, and the page text as the description; other columns become custom fields. Relations, images and attachments are not imported.
import-board-instruction-plane: In Plane, open Workspace Settings, choose Exports, export the projects as JSON, CSV or Excel and download the .zip file, then choose that file, or one file from inside it, or paste the JSON or CSV. States become lists, projects become swimlanes, and issues become cards with their identifier, parent, assignees, labels, dates, links and comments; priority, estimate, cycle and module become custom fields. Plane's export has no descriptions or attachments, so they are not imported.
import-board-instruction-fizzy: In Fizzy, export the account in Account settings, or your own cards with Download my data, and choose the .zip file Fizzy sends you, or one card's .json file. Boards become swimlanes and columns become lists, with Maybe?, Not now and Done as in Fizzy; cards keep their description, tags, assignees, steps as a checklist, comments and files.
import-board-instruction-mail: Choose an .mbox file, as Thunderbird, Apple Mail, mutt or Gmail through Google Takeout save it, or a single .eml message, or paste its text. Each conversation becomes one card in the Inbox list, with its sender, recipients and subject, so it shows in the Email view; the replies become its comments. Gmail labels become labels. Attachments are not imported.
import-board-instruction-ical: Choose an .ics calendar file, as Google Calendar, Apple Calendar or Reminders, Thunderbird, Nextcloud or Outlook export it, or paste its text. Tasks go to To Do, In Progress, Done or Cancelled by their status, and events to Events, with their start and due dates, so they show in the Calendar and Gantt views. Categories and priority become labels. Repeating items are imported once.
import-board-instruction-googletakeout: At takeout.google.com, choose Tasks, Keep, Mail, Calendar and Google Chat, create the export and download the .zip file, then choose it here. Each product becomes a swimlane: mail for the Email view, task lists and notes with their checklists, calendar events and tasks with dates, and chat spaces whose messages are comments for the Chat view. Other products and attachments are not imported.
import-board-instruction-slack: In Slack, open the workspace settings, choose Import/Export Data, export the workspace and download the .zip file, then choose it here. Each channel becomes a card in Channels, Groups or Direct messages, and its messages and thread replies become the card's comments, by their author, so the Chat view shows the channel. Files are not imported.
import-board-instruction-mattermost: Export with mmctl export create, download the export and choose its .jsonl file, or paste its text. Each channel and direct message becomes a card, and its posts and replies become the card's comments, so the Chat view shows the channel. Teams become swimlanes. Files are not imported.
import-board-instruction-telegram: In Telegram Desktop, open Settings, Advanced, Export Telegram data, choose the JSON format and export, then choose the result.json file, or paste its text. Each chat becomes a card in Direct messages, Groups or Channels, and its messages become the card's comments, so the Chat view shows the chat. Photos and files are not imported.
import-board-instruction-whatsapp: In WhatsApp, open the chat, choose Export chat without media, and choose the .txt file here, or paste its text. The chat becomes a card whose messages are its comments, by their sender and time, so the Chat view shows it. Media and system messages are not imported.
import-board-instruction-discord: Export a Discord channel with DiscordChatExporter in the JSON format and choose the .json file, or paste its text. The channel becomes a card in its category, and its messages become the card's comments, so the Chat view shows the channel. The server becomes the swimlane. Attachments are not imported.
import-board-instruction-rocketchat: In Rocket.Chat, export your data as JSON in My Data and choose the .zip file it sends you, or one room's exported .json file. Each room becomes a card and its messages become the card's comments, so the Chat view shows the room. The .zip that WeKan exports for Rocket.Chat's CSV importer is read too.
import-board-instruction-evernote: In Evernote, export the notes or a notebook as an .enex file and choose it here, or paste its text. Each note becomes a card with its text, its to-do checkboxes as a checklist, its tags as labels and its reminder as the due date; notes whose reminder is done go to Done. Images and attached files are not imported.
import-board-instruction-trello: In your Trello board, go to 'Menu', then 'More', 'Print and Export', 'Export JSON', and copy the resulting text.
import-board-instruction-csv: Paste in your Comma Separated Values(CSV)/ Tab Separated Values (TSV) .
import-board-instruction-jira: Paste the JSON of a Jira Cloud issue search: GET /rest/api/3/search/jql?jql=project=KEY&fields=*all&expand=names,schema (without fields it returns only issue ids). A large project comes in pages, each with a nextPageToken for the next: put the issues of every page into one "issues" array, or import each page as its own board with Import many boards. An equivalent { "issues": [...] } object works too. Jira statuses become lists and issues become cards. Optionally include an "automationRules" array to import rules.
import-board-instruction-excel: Choose an .xlsx workbook: a table with one card per row (columns such as Title, Description, Status/List, Members, Labels, dates and custom fields), or a workbook WeKan exported, also one with every board on a sheet of its own. The next step shows which column is which field. Every sheet with a header row becomes a board.
import-board-instruction-wekan: In your board, go to 'Menu', then 'Export board', and copy the text in the downloaded file.
import-board-instruction-about-errors: If you get errors when importing board, sometimes importing still works, and board is at All Boards page.

import-members-mode-placeholder: Keep them as placeholder users with their own names, to map to real users later

A .zip that is itself one export (Vikunja, Notion, Plane, or WeKan with attachments) is one board. When files are chosen here, Import imports them instead of the field above.
import-one-board-per-project-hint: Each swimlane the import would make (a project, folder or list of the tool) becomes its own board. Parent cards and dependencies between those boards are listed in the import report.
export-all-boards-hint: Every board you can export, in one download: Excel as one workbook with a sheet per board named after it, every other format as a .zip with a file per board.

import-trello-zip-unsafe-path: The .zip contains unsafe file paths and was rejected.

import-trello-workspace-placeholder: Imported board is placed under this workspace, created if it does not exist
trello-api-import: Import directly from Trello with API key and token

trello-api-token: Trello API token (manually generated below the API key)
trello-api-credentials-required: Please enter both the Trello API key and token.
trello-api-credentials-saved: Trello API key and token are saved. You can list workspaces without re-entering them.
trello-export-desc: Create a copy of this board in Trello through Trello's API, with your Trello API key and token. Swimlanes become labels named "Swimlane: …", which WeKan's Trello import turns back into swimlanes.

sandstorm-trello-save-label: Trello, for importing and exporting boards
trello-select-boards: Please select at least one board to import.
trello-cancel-delete-confirm: Cancel the import and delete the boards already imported by this job? This cannot be undone.

invalid-year: Invalid year. Please type all four digits, for example 2026.
just-invited: You are just invited to this board

label-delete-pop: There is no undo. This will remove this label from all cards and destroy its history.

hide-board: Leave this board: hide it from All Boards. Your team or organization membership stays, and Member Settings / Hidden boards brings it back.

leave-board-pop: Are you sure you want to leave __boardTitle__? You will be removed from all cards on this board.

list-move-cards: Move all cards in this list
list-select-cards: Select all cards in this list
list-delete-pop: All actions will be removed from the activity feed and you won't be able to recover the list. There is no undo.
list-delete-suggest-archive: You can move a list to Archive to remove it from the board and preserve the activity.
log-out-everywhere-confirm: This logs you out on every browser, phone and app where you are logged in, including this one.
passkeys-description: A passkey lets you sign in with this device's fingerprint, face, screen lock or security key instead of your password. It stays on your device; WeKan keeps only its public key.
passkey-add: Add a passkey on this device
passkey-invalid: That passkey could not be used.
passkey-sign-in-failed: Signing in with a passkey did not work. Try again, or sign in another way.
passkey-expired: That took too long. Try again.
passkey-too-many: You have the most passkeys an account can have. Remove one first.
passkey-needs-https: Passkeys need WeKan at an https:// address.
moveCardPopup-leave-link-at-origin: Leave a link at the original location
muted-info: You will never be notified of any changes in this board
name: Name

notify-participate: Receive updates to any cards you participate as creator or member
notify-watch: Receive updates to any boards, lists, or cards you’re watching
page-maybe-private: This page may be private. You may be able to view it by logging in.
paste-or-dragdrop: to paste, or drag & drop image file to it (image only)

board-instance-info: This board will be visible to every signed-in user.

custom-public-desc-placeholder: Leave empty to use the default public board description

remove-member-pop: Remove __name__ (__username__) from __boardTitle__? The member will be removed from all cards on this board. They will receive a notification.
sandstorm-remove-member-warning: This only hides the member inside WeKan. It does not revoke access to the Sandstorm grain. Revoke their access in Sandstorm's Share access dialog too.
rescue-card-description: Show rescue dialogue before closing for unsaved card descriptions
rescue-card-description-dialogue: Overwrite current card description with your changes?
search-cards: Search from card/list titles, descriptions and custom fields on this board
search-example: Write text you search and press Enter

set-wip-limit-value: Set a limit for the maximum number of tasks in this list
list-permissions-desc: What each role may do in this list, over what the board allows. Board admins can always edit.

set-default-board-title: Click to open this board automatically after you log in.

no-starred-items: You have not starred anything yet.

toggle-labels: Toggle labels 1-9 for card. Multi-Selection adds labels 1-9

custom-top-left-corner-logo-height: Custom Top Left Corner Logo Height. Default: 27

external-link-pattern-description: Autolinks "#1234"-style tokens found in card text to an external issue tracker. Leave either field empty to disable.
external-link-rules-description: One rule per line: the text to find, " = ", and the address. Use {number} for digits and {identifier} for a word, in both, for example [{identifier}:{number}] = https://tracker.example.com/{identifier}/{number}.
external-link-identifier-aliases: Abbreviations for {identifier}, for example TK=Task, IN=Incident
warn-list-archived: warning: this card is in an list at Archive
watching-info: You will be notified of any change in this board
what-to-do: What do you want to do?
wipLimitErrorPopup-dialog-pt1: The number of tasks in this list is higher than the WIP limit you've defined.
wipLimitErrorPopup-dialog-pt2: Please move some tasks out of this list, or set a higher WIP limit.

attachment-retention-purge: Remove deleted attachments for good after (days)
attachment-retention-purge-help: After this they can no longer be restored. Empty or 0: never.
attachment-retention-dry-run: Dry run: only count, in the server log, change nothing
attachment-retention-max-per-run: At most this many attachments per night

attachment-transfer-limits-invalid-value: Please enter a valid positive limit value
avatars-upload-blocked-description: Block users from uploading new avatars (useful when avatars are synced from another source). Avatars are enabled by default.

smtp-port-description: The port your SMTP server uses for outgoing emails.

send-smtp-test: Send a test email to yourself

email-smtp-test-text: You have successfully sent an email

webhook-payload-field-links: Links to the card and board
webhook-payload-field-people: The member or assignee it is about
webhook-payload-field-details: Details: comment, description, values and dates

sandstorm-sync-granted: This grain may reach this tracker

Sandstorm keeps them in the grant and signs every request in with them; WeKan never sees them.
webhooks-off-desc: Hides every webhook from the boards and the Admin Panel. The server sends no webhook and refuses to add or change one. Saved webhooks are kept and work again when this is turned off.
webhooks-report-desc: Every webhook of every board and every global webhook: who added it and what it sends. Tokens are not shown, only whether one is set.
webhooks-disabled: All webhooks are turned off in Admin Panel / Settings / Features.

read-only-field: Read-only: every member sees the value, only board admins change it
tableVisibilityMode-allowPrivateOnly: Boards visibility: Allow private boards only
org-tenant: Multitenancy: this Organization as a tenant
org-domains-description: Hostnames this Organization is served on, separated by commas — for example a.example.com, kanban.example.org. A request to one of them is this Organization's request, and the branding below replaces the instance branding for it. Only in effect when the server is started with MULTITENANCY=true. Leave empty when this Organization is not a tenant.
error-org-domain-taken: That domain already belongs to another Organization:
org-domains-requested: Requested by this Organization's admin, waiting for a site administrator to assign:
org-domains-request-saved: The new domains are saved as a request. A site administrator assigns them.
error-org-domain-reserved: That domain is this WeKan's own address and cannot belong to an Organization:

delete-all-notifications-confirm: Are you sure you want to delete all notifications? This action cannot be undone.
delete-duplicate-lists-confirm: Are you sure? This will delete all duplicate lists that have the same name and contain no cards.

r-wrike-workflow-note: A Wrike workflow is a list of statuses, each in the Active, Completed, Deferred or Cancelled group. Export writes this board's lists as one, named after the board, in the JSON Wrike's API returns for workflows: create that workflow in Wrike before importing the board's Wrike Excel export, so its statuses are applied. Import reads that JSON pasted above, from WeKan or from Wrike's GET /workflows, into the chosen board: a status without a list becomes a list, and a rule marks a card complete when it is moved into a Completed or Cancelled status and incomplete in an Active or Deferred one. Wrike's own automation rules cannot be exported from Wrike.

globalSearch-instructions-description: Searches can include operators to refine the search.  Operators are specified by writing the operator name and value separated by a colon.  For example, an operator specification of `list:Blocked` would limit the search to cards that are contained in a list named *Blocked*.  If the value contains spaces or special characters it must be enclosed in quotation marks (e.g. `__operator_list__:"To Review"`).
globalSearch-instructions-operator-board: `__operator_board__:<title>` - cards in boards matching the specified *<title>*
globalSearch-instructions-operator-list: `__operator_list__:<title>` - cards in lists matching the specified *<title>*
globalSearch-instructions-operator-swiml: `__operator_swimlane__:<title>` - cards in swimlanes matching the specified *<title>*
globalSearch-instructions-operator-label: `__operator_label__:<color>` `__operator_label__:<name>` - cards that have a label matching *<color>* or *<name>
globalSearch-instructions-operator-creat: `__operator_creator__:<username>` - cards where *<username>* is the card's creator
globalSearch-instructions-operator-org: `__operator_org__:<display name|short name>` - cards belonging to a board assigned to organization *<name>*
globalSearch-instructions-operator-team: `__operator_team__:<display name|short name>` - cards belonging to a board assigned to team *<name>*
globalSearch-instructions-operator-due: `__operator_due__:<n>` - cards which are due up to *<n>* days from now.  `__operator_due__:__predicate_overdue__ lists all cards past their due date.
globalSearch-instructions-operator-creat: `__operator_created__:<n>` - cards which were created *<n>* days ago or less
globalSearch-instructions-operator-modif: `__operator_modified__:<n>` - cards which were modified *<n>* days ago or less
globalSearch-instructions-operator-statu: `__operator_status__:<status>` - where *<status>* is one of the following:
globalSearch-instructions-operator-has: `__operator_has__:<field>` - where *<field>* is one of `__predicate_attachment__`, `__predicate_checklist__`, `__predicate_description__`, `__predicate_start__`, `__predicate_due__`, `__predicate_end__`, `__predicate_assignee__` or `__predicate_member__`.  Placing a `-` in front of *<field>* searches for the absence of a value in that field (e.g. `has:-due` searches for cards without a due date).
globalSearch-instructions-operator-sort: `__operator_sort__:<sort-name>` - where *<sort-name>* is one of `__predicate_due__`, `__predicate_created__` or `__predicate_modified__`.  For a descending sort, place a `-` in front of the sort name.
globalSearch-instructions-operator-limit: `__operator_limit__:<n>` - where *<n>* is a positive integer expressing the number of cards to be displayed per page.
globalSearch-instructions-notes-2:
Similar operators are *OR*ed together.  Cards that match any of the conditions will be returned.
`__operator_list__:Available __operator_list__:Blocked` would return cards contained in any list named *Blocked* or *Available*.
globalSearch-instructions-notes-3: Differing operators are *AND*ed together.  Only cards that match all of the differing operators are returned.  `__operator_list__:Available __operator_label__:red` returns only cards in the list *Available* with a *red* label.
globalSearch-instructions-notes-3-2: Days can be specified as a positive or negative integer or using `__predicate_week__`, `__predicate_month__`, `__predicate_quarter__` or `__predicate_year__` for the current period.
globalSearch-instructions-notes-5: By default archived cards are not searched.

cards-loading-description: WeKan loads board cards automatically: a big board (over the size threshold) loads only the cards currently visible (infinite scroll) plus a live count, so it stays fast and uses less memory and bandwidth, while smaller boards load every card for the simplest, fully featured experience. There is nothing to configure. Operators can still force a mode with the CARDS_LOADING (all/lazy/auto) and CARDS_LOADING_LAZY_THRESHOLD environment variables.
cards-loading-lazy-note: Lazy card loading is experimental: card counters and WIP limits are accurate, but the Calendar/Table/Gantt views and multi-select reflect only the cards loaded so far. Reload open boards after changing this.
render-links-as-plain-text-description: When enabled, all links (both markdown links like [label](url) and raw HTML <a href> tags) are always shown as plain, non-clickable text in every rich text field (board and card titles, descriptions, comments, checklists, etc.). This prevents misleading clickable links. Default is off, so links stay clickable.
always-show-code-as-text: Always show all code as plain text
always-show-code-as-text-description: When enabled, rich text is never rendered as markdown or HTML: the entire source is always shown as plain text in every rich text field (board and card titles, descriptions, comments, checklists, etc.). This reveals hidden content — HTML comments (<!-- -->), the target of markdown links, JavaScript and any other code — so all code is always visible, not clickable, and not running. Default is off, so markdown is rendered normally.
disable-all-import-description: When enabled, all import features are turned off: importing a board from WeKan JSON, Trello, CSV/Excel, Jira, Kanboard, NextCloud Deck, OpenProject, GitHub, GitLab, Gitea and Forgejo, as well as cloning a board. The import menu options are hidden and the server rejects any import request. Default is off.

disable-all-export-description: When enabled, all export features are turned off: exporting a board as WeKan JSON, CSV, Excel, Kanboard, or to NextCloud Deck / OpenProject / GitHub / GitLab / Gitea / Forgejo, and single-attachment export. The export menu options are hidden and the server rejects any export request. Default is off.
disable-import-avatars-description: When enabled, avatars (user profile pictures) are never imported. This covers WeKan JSON import, Trello import, and avatar sync from external identity providers on login (LDAP, OIDC/OAuth2). Names and other data are still imported; only avatars are skipped. Default is off.
disable-export-avatars-description: When enabled, avatars (user profile pictures) are never included when exporting a board (WeKan JSON and CSV export). Usernames and other data are still exported; only avatars are omitted. Default is off.
anonymize-import-users-description: When enabled, importing a WeKan JSON board replaces every imported user's username, full name and initials with counter placeholders (user1, user2, ...), drops their avatar, and rewrites @username mentions (and the requested-by / assigned-by fields) inside imported card and comment content. No real user identity from the source board is stored. The word "user" follows the language of the person importing. Default is off.
anonymize-export-users-description: When enabled, exporting a board replaces every exported user's username, full name and initials with counter placeholders (user1, user2, ...), drops their avatar, and rewrites @username mentions (and the requested-by / assigned-by fields) inside card and comment content. The exported file carries no real user identity. The word "user" follows the language of the person exporting. Default is off.
anonymize-account-confirm-popup: Are you sure you want to anonymize this account? This permanently replaces the username, full name and email address with anonymized placeholder values, removes the avatar, and disables login. Unlike delete, boards, cards and comments keep their history and still show this account, only anonymized. This action cannot be undone.
disable-activities-description: When enabled, activity-feed entries are never recorded and never shown anywhere (board sidebar and card activity tab). No history of who did what is kept. Default is off.
disable-notifications-description: When enabled, WeKan never sends watch notifications (in-app, email or other services) for any activity. Activities can still be recorded (unless also disabled above); only the notifications are suppressed. Default is off.
disable-watch-description: When enabled, the watch feature is turned off — users cannot subscribe to boards, lists or cards to receive notifications, and any attempt to change a watch level is rejected. Default is off.
backup-description: Back up Attachments, Avatars and/or Data (all text-based collections that are not attachments or avatars). The .zip is streamed directly to the selected storage — no temporary file — as backup/YYYY/MM/DD/HH_MM_SS/backup.zip, containing YYYY_MM_DD-HH_MM_SS/attachments, /avatars and /data. Cloud storages (S3/MinIO, Azure, GCS) use the credentials configured in their storage tabs.
backup-scope-description: The whole instance, or one Organization. An Organization's backup contains its boards and everything on them, including the attachments of those boards — but no user accounts and no instance settings, because those are shared by every Organization. Restoring an Organization's backup only ever writes to boards that Organization owns.

continuous-backup-description: Streams every change to the database, attachments, avatars and logs to a directory within seconds, so a restore can return to any moment. It runs beside the scheduled backup, which makes full archives.

blockly-TEXT_LENGTH_TOOLTIP: Returns the number of letters (including spaces) in the provided text.
blockly-TEXT_PRINT_TOOLTIP: Print the specified text, number or other value.
blockly-TEXT_PROMPT_TOOLTIP_NUMBER: Prompt for user for a number.
blockly-TEXT_PROMPT_TOOLTIP_TEXT: Prompt for user for some text.
blockly-TEXT_REPLACE_TOOLTIP: Replace all occurances of some text within some other text.
blockly-TEXT_REVERSE_TOOLTIP: Reverses the order of the characters in the text.
blockly-TEXT_TEXT_TOOLTIP: A letter, word, or line of text.
blockly-TEXT_TRIM_OPERATOR_BOTH: trim spaces from both sides of
blockly-TEXT_TRIM_OPERATOR_LEFT: trim spaces from left side of
blockly-TEXT_TRIM_OPERATOR_RIGHT: trim spaces from right side of
blockly-TEXT_TRIM_TOOLTIP: Return a copy of the text with spaces removed from one or both ends.
blockly-VARIABLES_GET_TOOLTIP: Returns the value of this variable.
blockly-VARIABLES_SET_TOOLTIP: Sets this variable to be equal to the input.
blockly-VARIABLE_ALREADY_EXISTS_FOR_ANOT: A variable named '%1' already exists for another type: '%2'.
blockly-VARIABLE_ALREADY_EXISTS_FOR_A_PA: A variable named '%1' already exists as a parameter in the procedure '%2'.
blockly-WORKSPACE_CONTENTS_BLOCKS_ONE: One stack of blocks%2 in workspace.
blockly-WORKSPACE_SEARCH_INPUT_LABEL: Search workspace. Press Enter for the next match, Shift+Enter for the previous match. Press Escape to close search and focus the current match.
r-blocks-help: Connect one trigger to one action. Drag blocks from the toolbox. Use the form editor for advanced options.
r-blocks-unavailable: Rule data is unavailable. Use the form editor to review this rule.
r-blocks-invalid: Connect exactly one trigger to one action. Remove disconnected or extra blocks before saving.
r-blocks-conflict: This rule changed while you were editing. Reload the saved rule before saving.
r-blocks-permission: Board administrator permission is required to edit rules.
scrum-edit-sprint: Create or edit a planned sprint
scrum-releases-select-help: A card can be in several releases. Hold Ctrl (Cmd on a Mac) to choose more than one; clear them all to remove the card from every release.
scrum-select-sprint: Select a sprint to view its report.
scrum-backlog-help: Order work by backlog rank. Assign cards to a planned or active sprint.
scrum-no-closed-sprints: No closed sprint snapshot is available.
scrum-report-help: Reports retain estimates from sprint snapshots. Unknown estimates are counted separately; they are not zero estimates. Compare velocity only across matching estimate units and policies.
scrum-confirm-close: Close this sprint and save its results? Unfinished cards will move to the selected destination.
scrum-confirm-cancel: Cancel this sprint? Its cards retain their membership until reassigned.
scrum-partial-report: Partial report: only cards currently assigned to you are included.
scrum-import-reference-omitted: A source reference could not be restored: __reference__
scrum-partial-snapshot: This sprint contains only part of the original snapshot.
scrum-rollover-progress: Moving the sprint's cards on: __done__ of __total__
scrum-history-job-running: Undoing or redoing a large change: __done__ of __total__ History rows
scrum-history-job-failed: A large undo or redo stopped. Press undo or redo again to continue it:
scrum-daily-observations-help: Each bar shows the first recorded observation of a UTC day, at the timestamp shown. Missing days are omitted. These observations do not record every change or show end-of-day totals. Unknown estimates are not zero. Use this section's Export action for daily observations; the toolbar Export action exports sprint results.
scrum-daily-truncated: Only the most recent 366 observations are shown.
scrum-daily-empty: No daily observations have been recorded for this sprint.
scrum-scope-history: Scope and burndown, change by change
scrum-scope-history-help: Replayed from the board's History since the sprint started: one row for each change to the sprint's cards, estimates or completed work.
scrum-scope-history-inconsistent: History does not reproduce this sprint's own snapshot: some changes were made without History, so these values are incomplete.
scrum-scope-history-truncated: Only the first changes could be read; the replay is incomplete.
scrum-scope-history-empty: No changes since the sprint started.
scrum-daily-observations-export-help: First recorded observation of each UTC day; missing days are omitted. Observations do not record every change or end-of-day totals. Unknown estimates are not zero.
scrum-import-pending: The Scrum import is incomplete. Scrum edits and report exports are unavailable.
scrum-import-recovery-hint: An import interrupted by a restart can be finished here once it has stopped. One whose plan was never fully saved can only be discarded, which changes nothing on the board.
scrum-import-into-board: Import Scrum planning into this board
scrum-import-into-board-hint: Choose a WeKan board export or Scrum transfer file. Sprints and releases this board already has are linked, never duplicated. Cards are matched by ID, or by card number and title; cards that do not match are listed and left unchanged. Preview first to see what will change.
scrum-import-invalid-file: This file is not valid JSON.
scrum-import-preview-sprints: Sprints: __created__ new, __matched__ already on this board, __skipped__ not imported
scrum-import-preview-releases: Releases: __created__ new, __matched__ already on this board, __skipped__ not imported
scrum-import-preview-cards: Cards: __updated__ to update, __unchanged__ unchanged, __unmatched__ not matched
scrum-import-preview-nothing: Nothing to change: this board already has this planning.
scrum-import-into-board-done: The Scrum planning was imported and recorded in History.
scrum-import-card-not-matched: A card was not found on this board: __reference__
scrum-import-card-ambiguous: A card matches more than one card on this board: __reference__
scrum-import-card-on-another-board: A card belongs to another board and was left unchanged: __reference__
scrum-import-record-ambiguous: A sprint or release matches more than one on this board: __reference__
scrum-import-record-not-imported: A sprint, release or event could not be imported: __reference__
scrum-import-sprint-finished: A card was not moved into a finished sprint: __reference__
sync-conflict-hint: Choose a value for each conflict. Sync retries after each choice. Nothing is sent to the source system.
sync-conflict-refresh: Run Sync again to review the current values.
sync-conflict-review-complete: Your assigned cards have been reviewed. No field conflicts remain. Full-list Sync was not run.
sync-conflict-detach: Keep duplicate as a local card
sync-conflict-detach-hint: Remove only this duplicate’s Sync mapping. Its content stays in WeKan.
sync-conflict-archive-hint: The source item is gone, but active subcards prevent archival. Keep this card locally by removing its Sync mapping. Subcards are not changed.
sync-conflict-creation-hint: Keep the previous card unchanged and create a new Sync card in this list. Retries reuse the replacement.
sync-preview-saved: Based on saved settings. Sync now fetches and checks the source again.
sync-preview-unavailable: Save a Sync source before requesting a preview.
sync-preview-blocked: Resolve the conflicts below before reviewing the change plan.
sync-preview-scope: Counts refer to normalized source fields. Additional data may be omitted by the source parser.
sync-source-scope: Paths group field occurrences across source items. Unmapped objects are reported as a whole; their values are not shown.
sync-source-converted: Converted to text or another representation
sync-source-fallback: Alternate value not used by the parser
sync-source-truncated: The report is limited to 100 paths and shortened field names.
sync-source-omitted: Additional occurrences outside the displayed paths
sync-report-retention: Latest 20 runs. Reports are retained for 30 days.
sync-report-partial: Failed or unfinished runs may have changed some cards. These reports do not resume or undo a run.
sync-report-unfinished: In progress or interrupted; outcome not recorded
sync-report-completed-with-warnings: Completed with omitted or converted fields
sync-report-unavailable: Run reports require full-list write access and an available server.
sync-recovery-description: Retained Sync reports from the last 30 days. Search by board or list ID. An unfinished outcome may still be running or interrupted. Refresh to check again; these reports cannot resume or undo changes.
sync-recovery-unavailable: Unable to read Sync diagnostics. Check administrator access and server availability.
sync-estimate-field-hint: Select a numeric field with a Jira field ID and estimate unit, as created by a mapped Jira import. Local changes are reviewed as conflicts. Missing source values are ignored; an explicit null clears the mapped value.
sync-estimate-field-gitlab-hint: GitLab's weight or time estimate is written to the numeric field you select. Local changes are reviewed as conflicts; an issue without a weight clears the mapped value.
email-recovery-description: One row per recipient. Search by user ID. Message content and recipient email fields are omitted. Pause holds existing and future messages; Resume retries queued messages now. Cancel removes messages queued up to the request time. If sending is busy, retry shortly. A message already being sent cannot be recalled, and uncertain delivery may be repeated. Permanent failures and exhausted retry limits remain available for review. Retry failed messages starts a new attempt cycle and respects an existing pause.
email-recovery-empty: No queued messages or paused recipients.
email-recovery-unavailable: Unable to read the email queue. Check administrator access and server availability.
email-recovery-busy: A delivery or another queue operation is in progress. Refresh and retry shortly.
email-recovery-failed: The operation could not be confirmed. Refresh the queue and retry the same action if needed.
email-recovery-superseded: A newer operator action has replaced this request. The current queue status is shown.
email-recovery-confirm-cancel: Cancel all currently queued messages for this recipient? Their contents will be removed and cannot be restored. New messages created after this request are kept.
email-failure-delivery-unconfirmed: Delivery could not be confirmed; review before retrying
email-failure-acknowledgement-failed: Delivery receipt could not be saved
sync-time-estimate-hint: Time estimates use the numeric original/remaining time fields created by Jira import. Exactly one matching field must exist on this board. Local edits are reviewed as conflicts; missing source values are ignored and explicit null clears the value.
sync-planning-hint: Sprint and releases are synced only while Scrum is enabled on this board. A sprint or release that is missing is created on this board, with the dates the source gives; an existing one is matched by its source ID first, then by name. A local planning change stays until the source changes that issue's planning, and a first Sync never removes planning.
activity-recovery-description: Unfinished notifications are retried automatically. Review missing or changed activities before retrying. Retrying never recreates an activity.
activity-recovery-unavailable: Could not load pending activity notifications.
activity-recovery-status-inconsistent: Plan and pending activity do not match
activity-recovery-busy: Another worker is handling this notification. Refresh and try again.
activity-recovery-denied: Recipient access or notification preferences no longer permit delivery.
activity-recovery-source-unavailable: The original activity is missing or has changed. Nothing was recreated.
activity-recovery-failed: Could not complete notification delivery. Pending work has been retained.
activity-recovery-control-conflict: This notification changed since it was loaded. Review the refreshed state before trying again.
activity-recovery-control-failed: Could not confirm the delivery setting. Refresh and review its current state.
activity-recovery-cancel-confirm: Permanently cancel remaining delivery for this activity? This cannot be resumed. Already queued email and delivered notifications are not recalled.
rule-email-recovery-description: Review recorded rule email attempts. Unconfirmed attempts may still be sending or may have been interrupted. This report does not retry or cancel delivery.
rule-email-recovery-empty: No rule email attempts match this search.
rule-email-recovery-unavailable: Could not load rule email attempts. Refresh to try again.
rule-email-recovery-actions-hint: WeKan never sends an unconfirmed email again by itself. Resend goes only to the recipients that are not confirmed. Mark it sent if you know it arrived, or drop it.
rule-email-recovery-wait: The original send may still be in progress. You can decide after __time__.
rule-email-recovery-resend-confirm: Send this email again to the unconfirmed recipients? Anyone whose mail server accepted it without WeKan being told will receive it twice.
rule-email-recovery-mark-sent-confirm: Mark this email as sent to everyone? Do this only if you know it arrived.
rule-email-recovery-drop-confirm: Drop this email? It will not be sent to the unconfirmed recipients.
rule-email-resolution-too-early: The original send may still be in progress. Try again later.
rule-email-resolution-already-resolved: This email has already been resolved.
rule-email-resolution-resend-in-flight: An earlier resend may still be in progress. Try again later.
rule-email-resolution-nothing-to-resend: Every recipient is already confirmed. Mark it as sent instead.
rule-email-resolution-resend-uncertain: The mail server did not answer. The resend may or may not have arrived; it is shown as in progress.
rule-email-resolution-busy: Another administrator is resolving this email. Try again shortly.
rule-email-resolution-command-changed: The stored email no longer matches this attempt, so it cannot be resolved here.
rule-email-resolution-attempt-invalid: This attempt's stored record is invalid, so it cannot be resolved here.
rule-email-resolution-failed: Could not resolve this email. Refresh and try again.
rule-email-legacy-description: These rule emails were prepared by an earlier WeKan version that did not record where their content came from, so WeKan will not send them by itself. Re-bind one to prepare it again from the card as it is now, after checking that the rule's author still has access, or discard it.
rule-email-legacy-reason-details-snapsho: Card details from an older version
rule-email-legacy-rebind-confirm: Prepare this email again from the card as it is now? Its content may differ from what was prepared before.
rule-email-legacy-discard-confirm: Discard this email? It will never be sent.
rule-email-legacy-empty: No rule emails are waiting for review.
rule-email-legacy-unavailable: Could not load the rule emails waiting for review. Refresh to try again.
rule-email-legacy-access-denied: The rule's author no longer has access to this card, or the rule has changed, so it cannot be re-bound. You can discard it.
rule-email-legacy-source-changed: The activity that triggered this email has changed, so it cannot be re-bound. You can discard it.
rule-email-legacy-source-unavailable: The card this email came from is no longer available, so it cannot be re-bound. You can discard it.
rule-email-legacy-plan-unavailable: The rule run that prepared this email is no longer stored, so it cannot be re-bound. You can discard it.
rule-email-legacy-attempt-exists: This email has already been sent, attempted or discarded.
rule-email-legacy-not-legacy: This email has already been re-bound.
rule-email-legacy-failed: Could not complete this action. Refresh and try again.
stuck-sync-operation-heading: List Sync operations that cannot be replayed
stuck-sync-operation-description: Each of these saved List Sync operations stopped part way and can no longer be finished, because its list was removed, recreated or reconfigured, or the user who started it lost write access. While one is pending, that list cannot Sync. Discard it to let the list Sync again: changes already applied stay, the remaining saved changes are never written, and the next Sync compares the list with its source again.
stuck-sync-operation-reason-scope-change: The list was removed, recreated or its Sync settings changed
stuck-sync-operation-reason-access-denie: The user who started it no longer has write access to the whole list
stuck-sync-operation-reason-trigger-unkn: Saved by an earlier WeKan version without what started it
stuck-sync-operation-reason-intent-missi: The record of who started it is missing
stuck-sync-operation-replayable-now: It can be replayed again now and will finish by itself, so it cannot be discarded.
stuck-sync-operation-discard-confirm: Discard this saved List Sync operation? Changes it already applied stay; the rest are never written. The list can then Sync again.
stuck-sync-operation-empty: No List Sync operations are waiting for review.
stuck-sync-operation-truncated: Only the oldest 50 are shown. Discard some and refresh to see more.
stuck-sync-operation-unavailable: Could not load the List Sync operations. Refresh to try again.
stuck-sync-operation-missing: This operation is no longer pending.
stuck-sync-operation-not-stuck: This operation has not been found stuck, so it cannot be discarded.
stuck-sync-operation-replayable: This operation can be replayed again now and will finish by itself, so it was not discarded.
stuck-sync-operation-busy: This list is syncing right now. Try again in a moment.
stuck-sync-operation-failed: Could not complete this action. Refresh and try again.
interrupted-import-heading: Board imports that stopped before finishing
interrupted-import-description: Each of these board imports stopped part way - the server restarted, or the import failed - and left a partial board. An import cannot be continued, because its source file is not kept. Keep the board as it is, or discard it and import the file again. Discarding removes the board this import created and everything on it, including anything added to it since.
interrupted-import-state-discarding: Being discarded; discard again to finish
interrupted-import-scrum: Its Scrum stage has its own checkpoint (__state__, __next__ of __total__ steps). If you keep the board, finish or discard it from the board's Scrum import recovery.
interrupted-import-counts: __swimlanes__ swimlanes, __lists__ lists, __cards__ cards, __checklists__ checklists, __comments__ comments, __attachments__ attachments
interrupted-import-keep-confirm: Keep this partial board as it is? Nothing is removed, and the import is no longer listed here.
interrupted-import-discard-confirm: Discard this import? The board it created and everything on it are removed permanently.
interrupted-import-empty: No interrupted board imports are waiting for review.
interrupted-import-truncated: Only the oldest 50 are shown. Keep or discard some and refresh to see more.
interrupted-import-unavailable: Could not load the interrupted board imports. Refresh to try again.
interrupted-import-missing: This import is no longer recorded.
interrupted-import-not-interrupted: This import is not waiting for a decision any more.
interrupted-import-foreign-board: The board with this id was not created by this import, so it was not touched.
interrupted-import-scrum-busy: Its Scrum stage is still being written or recovered. Try again in a few minutes.
interrupted-import-failed: Could not complete this action. Refresh and try again.
saml-login-not-started: This SAML sign-in was not started in this browser tab. Please sign in again.
history-request-pending-undo: Your last undo has not been confirmed by the server yet.
history-request-pending-redo: Your last redo has not been confirmed by the server yet.
history-request-hint: Trying again repeats the same request, so it can never take back a second change.
scrum-history-checkpoint-stuck: An undo, redo or restore of Scrum changes stopped on a conflict. Scrum edits on this board are blocked until it is resolved.
scrum-history-checkpoint-counts: __applied__ of __total__ changes were written, __pending__ were not, and __conflicted__ were changed by someone else since.
scrum-history-checkpoint-hint: Rolling back puts every changed record back as it was before; it is offered only when nobody else has changed those records since. Keeping the board as it is removes the stopped operation and changes no records. Either way, it is recorded in Admin Panel, Problems, Recovery.
scrum-history-checkpoint-discard: Keep the board as it is
scrum-history-checkpoint-discard-confirm: Keep every record as it is now, including the changes the stopped operation already wrote?
scrum-history-checkpoint-ask-admin: A board administrator can roll it back or keep the board as it is.
login-setting-clear-secret: Remove the value stored in the Admin Panel
login-setting-env-only: Only the server environment sets these. They are shown here read-only.
email-to-card-description: An email sent to your board address becomes a card on that board.
email-to-card-webhook: Mail provider inbound webhook URL (Mailgun, SendGrid, Postmark or a raw MIME relay)
email-to-card-secret-saved: Saved - leave empty to keep it
email-to-card-sandstorm-board: Board that email to this grain goes to
email-to-card-sandstorm-board-none: None - only emails with a board token in the subject
email-to-card-sandstorm-subject: Put this in the subject to reach this board as yourself:
email-to-card-parts: Parts of an email to use
email-to-card-part-sender-line: Sender line at the top of the description
email-to-card-your-address: Your email address for this board
email-to-card-address-private: Keep it private: anybody who has it can add cards as you.
email-to-card-new-address: New address (the old one stops working)
email-to-card-off-admin-off: Receiving email is not set up in the Admin Panel.
email-to-card-off-board-off: A board admin has not turned on email for this board.
email-to-card-off-member-off: You have turned your board addresses off in Member Settings.
email-to-card-off-sandstorm-no-session: The grain does not have its email address yet. Reload the page.
email-to-card-off-not-authorized: You need write access to this board.
inbound-domain-invalid: That is not a valid domain name.
inbound-domain-required: Give the domain of the board addresses.
inbound-account-invalid: An IMAP mailbox needs a valid server name.
feature-views-email-desc: The board as a mailbox: the email list is the Inbox, lists are folders, labels are labels, and members write and answer email from the board's address.
email-view-not-receiving: This board does not receive email yet. Turn it on in the board's Notification Settings → Email to card.
email-view-invalid-address: One of the addresses is not a valid email address.
email-view-too-many: Too many emails sent in the last hour. Try again later.
email-view-no-list: The board needs a list for the email.
email-view-send-failed: The email could not be sent.
feature-views-chat-desc: The board as a chat workspace: workspaces, boards, swimlanes, lists and cards as a tree of channels, the card in the middle and its comments as chat messages.
chat-view-pick-card: Pick a card from the channels to see it here.
chat-view-no-messages: No messages yet. Write the first one.
feature-views-column-sets-desc: The same cards in several named sets of columns - by completion, priority, milestone or anything else - moved between columns by dragging.
feature-rule-suggestions-desc: Board menu → Rules suggests rules from what people on the board keep doing by hand.
feature-board-summary-desc: Board menu → Summary shows what each person did on the board in the last day or week, and what they have overdue.
feature-since-last-visit-desc: Board menu → Since your last visit lists what others changed on the board since you last had it open.
feature-search-phrases-desc: Global search understands plain phrases such as "my overdue cards" and turns them into its operators.
column-sets-empty: No column sets yet. A board admin can make one: name it, then add its columns.
feature-views-version-control-desc: The board as a GitHub or Gitea issue tracker: cards as issues, labels and milestones, comments as the conversation, attachments as files, and the board history with undo.
vcs-no-milestones: No milestones yet. A label with a due date is a milestone.
vcs-no-list: This board has no list or swimlane for the issue.
card-qr-code-desc: Scan it to open this card on a phone or tablet.
card-qr-code-too-long: The link of this card is too long for a QR code.
vcs-no-wiki: No wiki yet. The GitHub organization import brings a repository's wiki here.
github-org-import-desc: Every repository of an organization or a user becomes its own board, opened in Board View / Version Control: its issues with their comments, labels and files, its releases, its GitHub Actions workflows as Rules, and its wiki.
github-org-import-token-hint: Needed for private repositories and a higher API limit. It is used only while the import runs and is never saved.
github-org-import-issues: Issues, with comments, labels and files
github-org-import-owner-invalid: Write an organization or user name, or its GitHub address.
github-org-import-running: An organization import is already running.
optional-apis-desc: REST APIs in the shape of other trackers' APIs, so that their apps and scripts can use this WeKan as their backend: what they save is stored in WeKan, on WeKan boards. Each one is off until ticked here. None has rights of its own: a client signs in with a WeKan API token and can see and change only what that person can see and change in WeKan. All of them need the WeKan REST API to be on (WITH_API=true). The address under each is what a client uses as its server.
optional-api-trello-desc: Apps and scripts written for Trello's REST API (for example Trellinator) work with WeKan: boards, lists, cards, labels, members, comments and checklists. The Trello token is a WeKan API token. Deleting a card archives it in WeKan.
optional-api-jira-desc: Clients of Jira's REST API v2 work with WeKan: a project is a board (its key is the board key), an issue is a card (DEV-7), a status is a list, and a transition moves the card. Search takes simple JQL: project, status, assignee = currentUser(), text and ORDER BY. Sign in with a WeKan API token as the password. Deleting an issue archives it.
optional-api-github-desc: Clients of GitHub's REST API for issues work with WeKan: a repository is a board, an issue is a card, with labels, milestones (labels with a due date), comments, and open or closed as in Board View / Version Control. The token is a WeKan API token.
optional-api-gitea-desc: Clients of Gitea's and Forgejo's REST API for issues work with WeKan, the same way as the GitHub-compatible API: a repository is a board and an issue is a card. The token is a WeKan API token.
bots-none: No bots yet. A bot is a runner on your own server - an AI agent, a CI job, a script - that this board hands cards to.
bot-not-found: That bot is not on this board.
bot-option-not-found: That answer is not one the bot offered.
webhook-internal-hosts-desc: Outgoing webhooks may not reach addresses on WeKan's own network, so that nobody can point a board's webhook at an internal service. List here the hosts on that network that webhooks may reach - a Node-RED, a chat server - one per line, as a name or an address, with a port to allow only that port. Empty: none. Only site administrators can change this list.
account-webhook-desc: One address that WeKan tells when somebody logs in or a new account is made. Nothing is sent until an event below is ticked. It carries the event, the user name and the time; tick more fields only if the receiver needs them.
account-webhook-on-register: When a new account is made
account-webhook-field-ip: IP address the login came from
activity-recovery-cancel-older-prompt: Cancel every pending notification of activities older than how many days?
vcs-synced-from: Synced from %s: open and close it there.
vcs-synced-issue: This issue is synced: open and close it in its tracker.
sync-write-back: Write changes back to GitLab: title, description, comments, closing and reopening
email-bounces-description: What WeKan does with email that comes back: a mistyped address, a full mailbox, an out-of-office reply, a spam complaint. Each kind has its own actions, done when it has bounced that many times.
email-bounces-category-hard-desc: The address does not exist: a typo, a deleted account, an unknown domain.
email-bounces-category-soft-desc: Not delivered for now: mailbox full, server busy. Only many in a row mean something.
email-bounces-category-auto-reply-desc: Out of office, vacation or ticket system replies. The email was delivered.
email-bounces-category-complaint-desc: The recipient marked the email as spam.
email-bounces-ses-description: In Amazon SES, send the Bounce and Complaint notifications, and a receipt rule for the address WeKan sends from, to an SNS topic, and subscribe this address to it over HTTPS:
email-bounces-ses-topics: SNS topic ARNs to accept, one per line
email-bounces-stopped-only: Only the addresses WeKan no longer emails
email-bounces-clear-hint: Forget this address's bounces and email it again
email-bounce-invalid-topic: That is not an SNS topic ARN.
email-bounces-providers-description: If WeKan sends through one of these services, turn it on, give the service this webhook address for its bounce and spam complaint events, and paste here the key it signs them with, or the password you put in the address as https://user:password@… or ?secret=…
email-bounce-provider-secret-required: A service that is turned on needs its signing key or password.
activity-pub-enabled: Public boards publish their card activity on the fediverse (ActivityPub)
activity-pub-desc: Off by default. With it on, each public board can be followed from Mastodon and other fediverse servers as @board-<id> at this WeKan's address, and new card activity reaches its followers. It is read-only: nothing a fediverse server sends changes a board, and private boards are never published.
caldav-sync-desc: Put this board's card due dates in a calendar - Nextcloud Calendar or any CalDAV calendar. A due date moved in the calendar comes back to the card. Use an app password, not your own.
caldav-enabled: Sync due dates with this calendar
caldav-invalid-url: The calendar address must be an http:// or https:// address, without a user name or password in it.
caldav-not-linked: Save a calendar address and turn sync on first.
webdav-storage-description: Store attachments in a folder on a WebDAV server - Nextcloud Files, ownCloud or any other. Use an app password made for WeKan. A server on WeKan's own network can be used here, since only a site administrator sets this address.
sqrl-desc: Off by default. With it on, the sign-in page offers SQRL, and members add their SQRL identity in Member Settings first. SQRL needs WeKan at an https:// address.
sqrl-scan: Scan the code with your SQRL app, or open your SQRL client on this device.
sqrl-expired: This SQRL code has expired. Start again.
sqrl-needs-https: SQRL needs WeKan at an https:// address.
sqrl-description: Sign in with your SQRL identity instead of a password. Add it here once with your SQRL client; you can remove it here at any time.
sqrl-disabled-by-client: SQRL sign-in is disabled for this account from your SQRL client. Re-enable it there with your rescue code.
sqrl-only-on: Your SQRL client has locked this account to SQRL: every other way of signing in is refused.
sqrl-hardlock-on: Your SQRL client has hardlocked this account: password reset and e-mail change are refused.
sqrl-only: This account signs in with SQRL only.
sqrl-hardlock: This account is locked to SQRL: it cannot be recovered or changed any other way.
windows-sso-failed: Windows sign-in failed. Your Windows account may not be allowed here.
enrollment-password-instructions: Confirm your password to start. This does not sign you in. An existing active factor cannot be replaced here.
enrollment-setup-denied: Cannot start setup. Check your credentials and whether one-time codes are already enabled.
enrollment-code-instructions: Use time-based codes: SHA1, six digits, 30 seconds. Keep the secret private. This setup expires in five minutes.
enrollment-confirmed-instructions: The confirmation code has been used. Wait for a new code in your authenticator before signing in.
registration-first-admin: This first account will be the Domain Global Admin.
auth-too-many-attempts: Too many login attempts. Try again later.
registration-global-admin-disabled: Global Admin accounts are initialized locally. Public registration is disabled.
registration-password-unavailable: Registration with a password is unavailable.
expedite-limit: Only one open card of a board can be Expedite at a time.
list-policy-placeholder: When may a card come into this list, and when is it done here?
commitment-point-hint: Work is committed to from this list on; the lists before it are options.
person-wip-over: __user__ has __count__ open cards; the WIP limit per person is __limit__.
feature-list-policies-desc: Each list's policy - when a card may come in and when it is done there - at the list header. Turned on per board in Board Settings / List.
feature-commitment-point-desc: The list from which work is committed to, marked at its header. Chosen per board in Board Settings / List.
feature-person-wip-limit-desc: How many open cards one person may hold on a board; an opened card warns about anyone over it. Set per board in Board Settings / List.
feature-standup-timer-desc: The board menu's Daily standup: the board's members in a shuffled order, each with the same timebox. Turned off per board in its Scrum settings.
feature-retrospective-board-desc: The board menu's Retrospective board: a new private board with the lists Start doing, Stop doing, Keep doing and Action items. Turned off per board in its Scrum settings.
show-split-lists: Allow lists split into Doing and Done
split-done: Done here, waiting to be pulled on
feature-split-lists-desc: A list split into Doing and Done: a card marked done there waits, dimmed, to be pulled into the next list, and the list header counts both. Allowed per board in Board Settings / List, then turned on in each list's menu.
workload-intro: The estimated hours and story points of the cards assigned to each person, week by week, against the hours they have: their working time, absences and public holidays. Click a week to see its cards.
workload-truncated: Too much to show at once: the report shows the first people and cards only. Choose fewer weeks or fewer boards.
workload-allocations-intro: How much of a person's time goes to a board, or which roles a board will need before anybody is named.
workload-invalid-estimate: The estimate must be between 0 and 10000 hours.
feature-workload-desc: The user menu's Workload and capacity: estimated hours and story points of each person's cards, week by week, against their working time, absences and public holidays, with allocations to boards and placeholder roles.
billing-intro: The boards you are an admin of: their budget, what their work has cost and will cost at the hourly rates you set, and invoices of the hours spent. Only board admins see this.
billing-no-boards: You are not an admin of any board.
billing-unrated: __hours__ h have no hourly rate and are not priced. Set a rate for the board or for those people.
billing-nothing-to-invoice: Every billable hour is already invoiced.
billing-set-rate-first: Set an hourly rate for this board first.
feature-billing-desc: The user menu's Budget and billing: a board's budget in money or hours, hourly rates, the cost and forecast of its work, and invoices of the billable hours spent. Only board admins see it.
billing-include-undated: Include time logged before dates were kept
billing-pay-by-scanning: Pay by scanning with your bank or payment app
billing-reverse-charge: Reverse charge: VAT is paid by the buyer
billing-undated-included: Includes __hours__ h logged before dates were kept.
billing-field-promptpay-target: Mobile number, national ID or e-wallet ID
billing-field-proxy: Mobile number, UEN, FPS ID or email
billing-uncosted: __hours__ h have no cost per hour and are not in the cost.
billing-bill-time: Bill time by the hour (off: a fixed price, only fees and expenses are invoiced)
billing-approve-time: Approve time before it is invoiced
billing-fees-intro: A milestone or a fixed price is billed once, from its day on; a retainer every month from its day until its end.
billing-nothing-to-approve: No time is waiting for approval.
billing-unapproved: __hours__ h are waiting for approval and are not on this invoice.
billing-quotes-intro: A quote prices the work still to do - each open card's estimate less the time spent - and the fees not invoiced yet.
billing-accept-sets-budget: Accepting a quote makes it the board's budget
workload-utilization-title: Billable hours logged against the working time of these weeks
